rule: Reading, source-record and collection clocks stay separate. Record lists and guides are labelled by kind; a linked reading does not prove every component of a multi-owner graphic.
presentation_qualifications: Swift shared ledger status (three statuses plus a headline): 4 readings disagree — World money record (dated rows) (September 29, 2025); Japan money map (September 15, 2026); UK legal map (on-ledger overlay) (September 14, 2026); Swift ledger page (crypto and networks master) (October 19, 2026). Unresolved; every reading is shown on this page.
S080's status is the most clearly out of date; S073 and S080 both cite Swift's '17 banks' release.
The rail names in the answer are the record's own; the master has no rail field, so rails are not counted one by one.

International room exception: rows may keep news links. Every row's url is the single link the page showed; 163 of the 164 page cards were labelled 'Reconstructed (not an official filing)' and 1 'Saved link'. Treat row urls as source_kind news unless the host is an official body.

DBS publication-date discrepancy: the official raw HTML and embedded publication field say September 7, 2026; its rendered public dateline shows September 6. The Library retains its saved September 7 label and records both source displays without inferring a timezone or correcting the issuer. Execution on September 5 is a separate clock.
The six count is published bilateral cases/pairings, not a census of individual transactions or recurring volume.
